newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Proposed NZ pension scheme is called CRSS - panel.
newsitem.headline: Proposed NZ pension scheme is called CRSS - panel.

text.p: The Independent Referendum Panel (IRP), charged with informing voters in the run-up to New Zealand's September referendum on superannuation, believes the government has got the name of the scheme wrong.

Speaking at a meeting on Thursday afternoon IRP chairman Sir John Robertson introduced the subject as the Compulsory Retirement Savings Scheme (CRSS), rather than the Retirement Savings Scheme (RSS), as it is called by the Treasury.
Driving home his point, which stems from the fact that there will be no way for workers to avoid contributing to the scheme if it is introduced, Robertson even put a questioner straight.
When asked about a detail of the RSS, the former ombudsman archly corrected him, "CRSS, isn't it?".

Treasurer Winston Peters, who has shepherded the scheme through its creation in the last half year, and who championed a public vote on the reform during last year's general election, had to accept introduction of the word 'compulsory' into the referendum question when it was finalised by MPs recently.
The ballot paper distributed for September's postal vote will read, "Do you support the proposed compulsory retirement savings scheme".

Although Robertson's IRP has no mandate to inform about alternatives to the CRSS scheme, he has said it intends to provide only facts about the proposals and not to present as facts any "glosses" the government has tried to place on it.
